title: Python SDK errors, accessors and misspelled names on the ZIA client

checks.do: Whether a failing call returns an error object or raises, since that is a client setting and not a property of the call.
Which spelling an attribute or method takes before writing it, because several are misspelled in the SDK and an expected name raises AttributeError.
Which SDK release a tenant script runs when a lite network-service field reads None.
That the accessor and method names in a script exist on the pinned SDK, rather than copying them from older notes.

accessor-new-instance.statement: The OneAPI client builds one `ZIAService` and keeps it, but each service property on that object (for example `user_management`) constructs a new API client object on every access; nothing is cached below the service object.

api-error-object.statement: A non-2xx REST response is turned into a `ZscalerAPIError` built from the URL, the response and the parsed body, and the request executor hands it back in the error slot. A response that is not JSON is returned as an `HTTPError` carrying the status code and body text.

raise-exception-flag.statement: The client setting `raiseException` defaults to False. When it is true the same API errors are raised as `ZscalerAPIException` (or `HTTPException`) instead of being returned in the error slot.

exception-classes-exist.statement: The Python SDK defines its own exception classes: `HTTPError` and `ZscalerAPIError` in `zscaler/errors`, `ZscalerAPIException` and `HTTPException` in `zscaler/exceptions`, and `RateLimitExceededError` in `zscaler/utils.py`.

dns-gateway-accessor-misspelled.statement: The unified ZIA service and the legacy ZIA client expose the DNS gateway client as the property `dns_gatways` (misspelled), imported from the module `zscaler/zia/dns_gatways.py`; no `dns_gateways` property exists on either.

browser-control-class-misspelled.statement: The browser control settings client class is spelled `BrowserControlSettingsPI` (no `A`), and the unified service and the legacy client both import and return it under that name; the property is spelled correctly as `browser_control_settings`.

custom-file-type-getter-misspelled.statement: The custom file types client names its single-item getter `get_custom_file_tytpe` (misspelled); it has no `get_custom_file_type`, which is the name a reader would expect.

l10n-key-corruption-fixed.statement: Before Python SDK 1.9.22, response keys with a digit-letter boundary such as `isNameL10nTag` or `ipV6Enabled` were re-cased by a generic camel-case helper (`L10n` became `L10N`), so the model field came back as `None`. The release replaced the normalizer with the SDK's own `to_lower_camel_case`, and the current response formatter uses it.

quotes: camelCase response keys with digit/letter boundaries (e.g. `isNameL10nTag`, `ipV6Enabled`) were silently corrupted by `APIClient.form_response_body()`

network-services-lite-model.statement: Release 1.9.22 gave `list_network_services_lite()` a dedicated `NetworkServicesLite` model with a nested `NetworkServiceExtensions` block that exposes the `extensions.tag` payload.

quotes: Added a dedicated `NetworkServicesLite` model (with a nested `NetworkServiceExtensions` block) for the ZIA `/networkServices/lite` endpoint

url-filtering-accessor.statement: The URL Filtering rules client is the `url_filtering` property of the ZIA service (not `url_filtering_rules`), and its rule methods are list_rules, get_rule, add_rule, update_rule and delete_rule.

categories-accessor.statement: The URL categories client is the `url_categories` property, with list_categories, get_category and delete_category among its methods.

activation-accessor.statement: Activation is `client.zia.activate` with `status` and `activate` methods, not `client.zia.activation` with `get_status`.
